newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX ELECTRIC FUTURES CALLED LOWER WITH OTC, CASH.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX ELECTRIC FUTURES CALLED LOWER WITH OTC, CASH.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were called to open lower Wednesday in line with weaker daily and over-the-counter (OTC) prices due to moderate demand and rising spot supply due to to units returning to service.
"Cash prices are getting hit pretty hard," a Houston futures trader.

Firm peak power prices for Thursday at Palo Verde (PV) fell more than $10.00 in early trading to $29.00-30.00 a megawatt hour (MWh), while those at California-Oregon Border (COB) slipped about a dollar to $20.00-21.00.

In OTC business, September PV futures were quoted at $29.50-29.90 a MWh down from Tuesday's settlement at $30.51, and September COB was discussed at $22.00-22.30 down from yesterday's close at $23.10.
On Tuesday, September PV gapped at $31.30-31.75 and September COB $22.90-23.60.
Analysts pegged chart support for September PV at $30.25 and for September COB at $21.40.
Forecasters called for cool, dry weather in the northern section of the Southwest the rest of week and seasonal conditions in the rest of the region with chance of rain and thunderstorm.
In the Pacific Northwest, temperatures would run as low as 12 degrees F below normal in the interior area, while those along the coast would average near to slightly above normal.
In generation news, power production at the 1,139 megawatt (MW) WNP-2 nuclear plant in Washington state was reduced briefly because an adjustable speed drive for a recirculation pump malfunctioned.
A 670 MW unit at the Centralia coal-fired plant in Washington state was expected to be back on line today after shutting Monday for repairs.
Restart of the 750 MW unit 3 at the Navajo coal-fired power plant near Page, Ariz., was delayed to Tuesday afternoon due to a boiler tube leak.
The unit, which was shut over the weekend for repairs, had been expected to restart late Monday. Navajo's other two 750 MW units were said to be operating normally.
The 700 MW unit 4 at the Colstrip coal-fired power plant in Montana was also scheduled to restart Tuesday afternoon after being shut Friday for unplanned repairs.
The plant's other 700 MW unit, as well as two smaller 330 MW units, were said to be operating normally.
Separately, southbound transmission capacity on the Pacific Intertie will be cut by 350 MW to 850 MW during certain hours today, according to the Bonneville Power Administration (BPA).
